final:
I rewrote `/agent/solver.md`. All three trials still failed, so I have no evidence yet that the change raises the pass rate.

**What the report showed:** most failures came from the agent stopping too early. The solver usually used only 2–4 of its 16 model calls. Of the 34 failures, 19 submitted a program that already failed the public examples. It often submitted right after a failing test run, or submitted code different from what it had tested. Several times it gave up in plain text ("I can't derive a solution"), which ended the run.

**What the new prompt says:**
- **Every reply is a tool call:** nothing in plain text before submitting, and never give up.
- **Pre-submit check:** only submit code that just passed every public example in exactly that form; keep debugging until about 13 calls are used.
- **Workflow:** write a brute-force version first, compare it against the fast solution on random small inputs, time it on a maximum-size input, then check edge cases.
- **Time limits:** rough limits for what input sizes Python can handle at each complexity, plus common faster techniques.

**Trials:**
- **lcb-arc194-a, first version:** the agent gave up in text after 3 calls. This is why I added the "every reply is a tool call" rule.
- **lcb-arc194-a, second version:** it debugged a little, then submitted a program that still failed the examples, after 4 calls.
- **lcb-arc184-c, final version:** it used 8 calls and actually explored the problem, but still submitted a program that failed an example.

So it now uses more of its budget, but it still sometimes ignores the "don't submit failing code" rule. `validate()` passes.
